name: Somax First Steps Full Body
description: A confidence-building full-body session using machines and dumbbells so you can learn the movement patterns before loading a barbell.
whoItsFor: Complete beginners in a commercial gym who want a simple plan they can follow without a coach, around a busy week.
howToRun: Mon/Wed/Fri or any 3 days with a rest day between.
Pick weights that leave 2-3 reps in the tank; when you hit the top of the rep range on every set, go up the next increment.
Rest 60-90s between sets.
After 8-12 weeks, move to Somax Strength Foundations or StrongLifts 5x5.

name: Somax Home Dumbbell Full Body
description: A full-body muscle-building session with just a pair of dumbbells, paired into supersets to save time.
whoItsFor: Beginners training at home with one or two pairs of dumbbells - ideal for parents, shift workers or anyone who can't get to a gym.
howToRun: 3 days a week, non-consecutive.
Use a weight you can lift for the top of the range with 1-2 reps to spare; add reps first, then weight.
Rest 60s after each superset round.
When the heaviest dumbbells feel light for 15 reps, slow the lowering to 3 seconds or move to a gym plan.

name: Somax Strength Foundations
description: A barbell session with one heavy top lift, a lighter second lift and targeted accessories - the bridge from beginner linear progress to wave loading.
whoItsFor: Lifters 6-18 months in who have stalled on a beginner 5x5 and can train three times a week around work.
howToRun: 3 days a week; rotate the main lift (squat, bench, deadlift, press) each session.
Work up to a top set of 5 at RPE 8, then 3 back-off sets at 90% of that weight. Add 2.5kg to the top set when it moves well.
Rest 3 min on main lifts, 90s on accessories.
Every 4th week take a lighter deload week.

name: Somax Upper Builder
description: Chest, back, shoulders and arms with a heavier compound start and supersets to finish. Pairs with Somax Lower Builder.
whoItsFor: Intermediate gym-goers who want to build muscle on four days a week without spending hours per session.
howToRun: Upper/Lower/rest/Upper/Lower/rest/rest (e.g. Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri).
Double progression: when all sets hit the top of the rep range, add 2.5kg (or the next dumbbell).
Rest 2 min on the first two lifts, 60-90s on supersets.
After 8-12 weeks, move to a push/pull/legs split for more volume.

name: Somax Lower Builder
description: Quads, glutes, hamstrings and calves: a heavy squat, a hinge, then single-leg and machine work.
whoItsFor: Intermediate gym-goers on a four-day upper/lower split who want stronger, bigger legs.
howToRun: Run with Somax Upper Builder: Upper/Lower x2 per week.
Add 2.5-5kg to squat and RDL when you hit the top of the range on all sets.
Rest 2-3 min on squats and RDLs, 60-90s elsewhere.
Deload every 5th-6th week.

name: Somax Heavy Singles Power Day
description: A peaking-style day for experienced lifters: a long warm-up ladder, heavy singles, then volume back-offs and minimal accessories.
whoItsFor: Advanced lifters (2+ years, solid technique) training for a powerlifting meet or a new max. Needs a proper rack with safeties.
howToRun: Use once a week per main lift within a 4-day plan.
Work up in small jumps to a single at RPE 8-9 - never a grinder. Then 3x3 at ~85% of today's single.
Rest 3-5 min between heavy sets.
Run 3 weeks heavier, then 1 lighter week. Test maxes no more than every 8-12 weeks.

exercises.name: Warm-up: bike + hip and thoracic mobility

name: Somax Advanced Push Hypertrophy
description: High-volume chest, shoulder and triceps work with a drop set and supersets for experienced lifters chasing size.
whoItsFor: Advanced lifters running a 6-day push/pull/legs split who recover well and want more volume than a beginner PPL.
howToRun: Use in a PPL-PPL-rest week.
Leave 1-2 reps in reserve on compounds; take isolation work close to failure.
Rest 2-3 min on presses, 60s on isolation and supersets.
Add a set to one exercise every 2 weeks, then deload and reset volume every 6-8 weeks.

name: Somax Kettlebell Express
description: A 25-minute one-bell session: swing and goblet squat practice, then an EMOM of presses, rows and carries.
whoItsFor: Busy people with one kettlebell and the basic swing already learned, training at home or in a hotel.
howToRun: 3 non-consecutive days a week.
Pick a bell you can press 5 times per arm with good form.
In the EMOM, start each exercise at the top of the minute and rest for the rest of it.
When the EMOM leaves you 25s+ rest every minute, move to a heavier bell.

name: Somax Low-Impact HIIT 20
description: A joint-friendly interval session with no jumping: 30 seconds on, 30 seconds off, done quietly in a living room.
whoItsFor: Beginners, larger bodies, people with sore knees, and anyone in a flat where jumping isn't an option.
howToRun: 3 days a week, non-consecutive.
Work at a 6-7/10 effort; you should be breathing hard but in control.
Rest 30s between moves; 60s between rounds.
Progress to 40s on / 20s off, then to the 7-Minute Workout.

name: Somax Dumbbell Fat-Loss Circuit
description: A full-body dumbbell circuit that keeps your heart rate up while still training every muscle - strength and conditioning in one.
whoItsFor: Intermediate exercisers who want to lose fat while keeping muscle, with only 35 minutes and a set of dumbbells.
howToRun: 3 days a week; walk on rest days for extra activity.
Move straight from one exercise to the next; rest 90s after each round.
Add a 5th round, or go heavier, once 4 rounds feel manageable.
Pair with a modest calorie deficit and enough protein for real fat loss.

name: Somax Advanced Engine Metcon
description: A demanding conditioning session: rower sprints followed by a 20-minute AMRAP of kettlebell and gymnastics work.
whoItsFor: Very fit people with solid technique on swings, pull-ups and box jumps who want maximum conditioning in under an hour.
howToRun: No more than 2 times a week, at least 48h apart.
Row intervals at near-max effort; the AMRAP at a pace you can hold for the full 20 minutes.
Rest 90s between row sprints.
Track rounds completed and try to beat it in 3-4 weeks.

name: Somax Bodyweight Starter 20
description: A 20-minute no-equipment session that teaches the basic squat, push, hinge and plank patterns.
whoItsFor: Complete beginners and returning exercisers who want to start at home with nothing but a chair.
howToRun: 3 days a week, e.g. Mon/Wed/Fri.
Add 2 reps per set each week until you reach 15, then move to the harder version (e.g. floor push-ups).
Rest 45-60s between rounds.
When everything feels easy at 15 reps, move on to the r/bodyweightfitness Recommended Routine.

name: Somax Calisthenics Skill & Strength
description: Skill practice (handstand and L-sit) while fresh, then harder strength pairs: pull-ups, dips, pistol progressions and core.
whoItsFor: Intermediate bodyweight trainees who can do at least 5 pull-ups and 10 push-ups and want to work toward skills. Great for park or home training.
howToRun: 3 days a week with rest days between.
Skill work: short, perfect holds - stop before form breaks.
Strength pairs: when you hit 3x8, add weight or move to a harder progression.
Rest 90s between paired exercises.

name: Somax Advanced Calisthenics Strength
description: Weighted pull-ups and dips, front-lever and planche progressions, and unilateral leg strength for very experienced athletes.
whoItsFor: Advanced calisthenics athletes (15+ pull-ups, 20+ dips) who train skills seriously and want structured strength work.
howToRun: 4 days a week (upper/lower or two full-body pairs).
Weighted work at RPE 8; add 1-2.5kg when all sets hit the top of the range.
Rest 2-3 minutes between heavy sets; skills before strength.
Deload every 5th week; retest max holds every 6-8 weeks.

name: Somax Easy Run & Strides
description: A relaxed conversational run with short, fast strides at the end to build easy speed and good form.
whoItsFor: New runners who can already run 20-30 minutes non-stop (e.g. Couch to 5K graduates).
howToRun: 3 runs a week; keep at least 2 of them fully easy.
Easy = you can talk in full sentences.
Strides: 20s quick but relaxed, walk back to recover.
Add 5 minutes to one run per week, no more than ~10% total weekly increase.

name: Somax Tempo Run
description: A sustained 'comfortably hard' run that lifts your lactate threshold - the key session for faster 5K-half marathon times.
whoItsFor: Runners covering 20+ km a week who want to race faster.
howToRun: Once a week, with easy runs either side.
Tempo pace: around your 10K-to-half-marathon pace, 7/10 effort - you can speak a few words only.
Build from 2x8 min to 2x12 min or 20-25 min continuous over 6-8 weeks.
Don't race the tempo; finishing feeling you could do more is right.

name: Somax Track 800s
description: Classic VO2max intervals: six 800m repeats at around 5K race pace with equal-time jog recoveries.
whoItsFor: Experienced runners (30+ km/week, consistent for a year) training for 5K-10K races.
howToRun: Once a week; never on back-to-back days with another hard session.
Run each rep at 5K race pace; the last rep should match the first.
Jog 400m (or 2-3 min) between reps.
Progress to 8x800m, then to 5x1000m.

exercises.name: Drills: A-skips, high knees, butt kicks

name: Somax Runner's Strength
description: Single-leg strength, calf and hip work and a little plyometrics to make runners more resilient and economical.
whoItsFor: Runners of any distance who currently do no strength work, training at home or in a gym twice a week.
howToRun: 2 sessions a week, ideally on easy-run days (after the run) - not before a key workout.
Use dumbbells that make the last 2 reps hard; add weight when all reps are smooth.
Rest 60-90s.
Reduce to 1 session a week in the last 10 days before a race.

name: Somax Brisk Walk & Hills
description: A brisk walk with short uphill or fast-pace intervals to raise your heart rate without running.
whoItsFor: Beginners, older adults, and anyone who prefers walking to running and wants more from their daily walk.
howToRun: 4-5 days a week; this is the hard walk - make the other walks easy.
Push sections: walk fast or uphill until slightly breathless but able to talk.
Add one push interval per week up to 8.
Once 8 intervals are easy, try Couch to 5K.

name: Somax Indoor Endurance Ride
description: A steady zone-2 ride with gentle cadence drills - builds the aerobic base everything else sits on.
whoItsFor: New cyclists, gym exercise-bike users, and anyone who wants low-impact cardio at home.
howToRun: 2-4 times a week.
Zone 2: you can hold a conversation; nose breathing is a good check.
Add 5-10 minutes per week to the steady block.
When 60 minutes is comfortable, add British Cycling's 20-min warm-up efforts or the 2x20 session.

name: Somax Cycling VO2 Intervals
description: Five hard 4-minute efforts just above threshold to push your aerobic ceiling, for riders who already train with power or heart rate.
whoItsFor: Experienced cyclists training for racing, crits or hilly sportives, who know their FTP or max HR.
howToRun: Once a week in build phases; never two days in a row.
Efforts at 106-120% FTP (or 90-95% max HR); recover at under 55% FTP.
If you can't hold power on the 4th rep, stop the session there.
Progress from 4x4 to 5x5 minutes over 6 weeks.

name: Somax Swim Confidence Builder
description: Short lengths with plenty of rest, kick and breathing drills to build comfort in the water.
whoItsFor: Adults who can swim a length but get out of breath quickly, or are returning to swimming after years away.
howToRun: 2 swims a week.
Rest 20-30s (or as long as you need) after each length.
Breathe out steadily underwater; turn the head to breathe rather than lifting it.
When you can do 4x50 with 20s rest, move to the USMS Quick Hit.

name: Somax Swim Endurance Builder
description: A 2,000m aerobic session with a descending main set and pull work for steady endurance.
whoItsFor: Swimmers comfortable with 1,000m+ continuous freestyle, including triathletes in base training.
howToRun: 2-3 swims a week.
Main set: hold an even pace; descend effort 1-3 within each round.
Rest 15-20s between 100s.
Shorten rest by 5s every two weeks, then add a round.

name: Somax Soccer Speed & Power
description: Acceleration, change of direction and lower-body power, built on a FIFA 11+-style warm-up to keep hamstrings and knees healthy.
whoItsFor: Amateur and youth soccer players (14+) who want to be quicker over the first 10 metres and stronger in duels, off a pitch or field.
howToRun: 2 sessions a week in-season, not within 48h before a match.
Sprints are maximal with full recovery (walk back + 60s); stop if speed drops.
Land jumps softly with knees tracking over toes.
In pre-season, add a third session and increase sprint reps by 2.

name: Somax Basketball Jump & Agility
description: Vertical jump, landing mechanics, lateral quickness and ankle-knee resilience for hoopers.
whoItsFor: Teen and adult basketball players who want to jump higher and move better laterally, training around team practice.
howToRun: 2 sessions a week, away from the day before games.
Keep jump reps low and every rep explosive; rest 60-90s between jump sets.
Add load to squats/RDLs when all reps are crisp.
Taper to one lighter session in heavy game weeks.

exercises.name: Dynamic warm-up: skips, lateral shuffles, leg swings

name: Somax Tennis Footwork & Rotational Power
description: Split-step footwork, rotational med-ball power and shoulder care to support faster movement and stronger groundstrokes.
whoItsFor: Club and junior tennis players who want better court speed and fewer shoulder issues, training twice a week alongside hitting.
howToRun: 2 sessions a week, ideally after a hitting session or on non-match days.
Med-ball throws: maximum intent, full rest between sets.
Shoulder band work is light - it should never cause pain.
Before tournaments, keep only the warm-up and band work.

exercises.name: Split-step to First Step (react to call)
Rotational Med Ball Throw (side to wall)

name: Somax Boxing Conditioning
description: Boxing-round conditioning: skipping, heavy-bag combinations and bodyweight finishers on a 3-minute work, 1-minute rest clock.
whoItsFor: People who train boxing or want boxing-style fitness, with access to a bag (gym or garage).
howToRun: 3 times a week, non-consecutive.
Keep hands up and breathe out on every punch; quality beats volume.
Rounds: 3 min on, 1 min off; drop to 2 min rounds if you're new.
Add a bag round every 2 weeks up to 8.

name: Somax Shadow Boxing Starter
description: Learn stance, guard and basic punches through 2-minute shadow-boxing rounds with simple bodyweight moves between.
whoItsFor: Beginners who want fun cardio at home with no equipment, including those curious about starting boxing.
howToRun: 3 times a week.
2-minute rounds, 1 minute rest; stay light on your feet.
Punch at speed but never lock the elbows.
When 6 rounds feel easy, move to 3-minute rounds or Somax Boxing Conditioning.

name: Somax Golf Mobility & Rotation
description: Hip and thoracic mobility plus rotational strength so you can turn more freely and swing with less strain on your lower back.
whoItsFor: Golfers of all ages - including older players - who feel stiff in the swing, training at home twice a week.
howToRun: 2 sessions a week at home; do the 5-minute warm-up before every round.
Move into stretches slowly and breathe; hold end range 2 seconds on rotations.
Add band resistance once the movements feel easy.
Pain in the lower back means reduce range and seek advice.

name: Somax Hybrid Starter
description: A taste of hybrid racing: short run or erg intervals alternating with simple strength stations.
whoItsFor: Gym-goers curious about HYROX-style events who can jog 15-20 minutes and want an approachable first step.
howToRun: 2 times a week alongside normal training.
Run/erg at a steady 6/10 effort; stations controlled, not rushed.
Rest 1 minute between rounds.
After 6 weeks, add a 4th round and move toward Somax Hybrid Race Prep.

name: Somax Hybrid Race Prep
description: Race-pace compromised running: 1km repeats straight off the hardest HYROX stations to train running on tired legs.
whoItsFor: Experienced hybrid athletes 6-12 weeks out from a HYROX-style race.
howToRun: Once a week; the other sessions should be easy runs and strength.
Run at goal race pace; stations at race standard.
Rest 2 minutes between rounds.
Do the full race simulation 3-4 weeks before race day, then taper.

exercises.name: Rotating station: sled push / burpee broad jump / sandbag lunge / wall balls

name: Somax Pilates Core Foundations
description: Beginner-friendly mat Pilates with modified versions of the classical exercises: breathing, pelvic control and gentle core work.
whoItsFor: Pilates newcomers, desk workers with stiff backs and older adults who want controlled core work at home.
howToRun: 3 times a week.
Move slowly; keep the lower back gently in contact with the mat during abdominal work.
Add 2 reps per exercise every couple of weeks.
When these feel easy, move to the Classical Mat Pilates First Fifteen.

name: Somax Mobility Reset 15
description: A daily 15-minute routine for hips, spine and shoulders - perfect after a day at a desk or as a rest-day session.
whoItsFor: Anyone stiff from sitting, travelling or training - busy people, older adults and lifters on rest days.
howToRun: Daily or on rest days.
Hold each stretch with slow nasal breathing; ease off if anything pinches.
Gradually increase holds from 30s to 60s.
Combine with the Sun Salutation for a longer flow.

name: Somax Deep Flexibility Flow
description: End-range strength and long holds for splits, pancake and overhead mobility - flexibility you can actually use.
whoItsFor: Experienced trainees, martial artists, dancers and climbers who already stretch regularly and want advanced flexibility.
howToRun: 3 times a week, not before heavy leg training.
Active end-range work: contract at the end of the stretch for 5-10s, then relax deeper.
Never force range; aim for a 6/10 stretch intensity.
Track range monthly (e.g. hands-to-floor in pancake).

name: Somax Strong & Steady
description: Strength and balance for everyday life: sit-to-stands, step-ups, rows and balance holds with a chair for support.
whoItsFor: Older adults and people new to exercise who want to stay strong, steady on their feet and independent.
howToRun: 2-3 times a week on non-consecutive days.
Hold a chair or counter for balance work; progress by lightly touching, then letting go.
Build to 12-15 reps before adding a band or heavier weight.
Stop and seek advice if you feel dizzy or have chest pain.

name: Somax Hotel Room Full Body
description: A no-equipment workout that fits a hotel room: slow-tempo strength supersets and a short finisher.
whoItsFor: Frequent travellers and busy professionals who want to keep training on the road with nothing but the floor and a chair.
howToRun: Use 2-3 times a week while travelling.
Use a 3-second lowering phase to make bodyweight harder.
Rest 60s after each superset.
Back home, return to your normal gym plan - this keeps your fitness ticking over.

exercises.name: Tempo Bulgarian Split Squat (rear foot on bed/chair)
